# NES controller connection issue
I see you recently added support for them; which pins do they connect to? I'm going to make my own connector with a breadboard and a voltage logic level converter.

6 7 8 9 NESTang is an open source project to recreate the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) with Sipeed Tang FPGA boards, including Sipeed [Tang Primer 25K](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-primer-25k/primer-25k.html), [Tang Nano 20K](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-nano-20k/nano-20k.html) and [Tang Primer 20K](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-primer-20k/primer-20k.html). 10 11 Main features, 12 13 - 720p HDMI output with sound. 14 - Cycle accurate gameplay quality has been achieved since the NES circuits have been almost entirely replicated. 15 - Rom loading from MicroSD cards with an easy-to-use menu system. 16 - Playstation 2 controllers support and experimental USB gamepads support. 17 18 ## Pick a Board 19 20 You need either the Sipeed Tang Primer 25K or Tang Nano 20K FPGA board to run the latest NESTang. 21 22 * The Tang Primer 25K is the latest small-form-factor, modular FPGA board from Sipeed. If you want more memory and extensibility, choose Primer 25K. You need to get the [main Primer 25K dock board](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-primer-25k/primer-25k.html), [DVI PMod](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-PMOD/FPGA_PMOD.html#PMOD_DVI), [TF Card PMod](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-PMOD/FPGA_PMOD.html#PMOD_TF-CARD), [DS2x2 PMod](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-PMOD/FPGA_PMOD.html#PMOD_DS2x2) and a [Tang SDRAM](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-PMOD/FPGA_PMOD.html#TANG-40P-MODULE). 23 * The Tang Nano 20K is a tiny and popular FPGA dongle. The board also features 8MB of FPGA-gaming-friendly SDRAM memory. Be sure to get the [Tang Nano 20K Retro Gaming Kit](https://www.amazon.com/GW2AR-18-Computer-Debugger-Multiple-Emulator/dp/B0C5XLBQ6C), as it contains the necessary controllers and adapters. 24 25 ## Installation 26 ### Code Snippet 1: verilator/README.md 3 To run the simulation: 4 5 ### Code Snippet 2: 10 11 You need to set up verilator / libsdl2 with something like: 12 13 ### Code Snippet 3: 20 ### Code Snippet 4: README.md 19 20 You need either the Sipeed Tang Primer 25K or Tang Nano 20K FPGA board to run the latest NESTang. 21 22 * The Tang Primer 25K is the latest small-form-factor, modular FPGA board from Sipeed. If you want more memory and extensibility, choose Primer 25K. You need to get the [main Primer 25K dock board](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-primer-25k/primer-25k.html), [DVI PMod](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-PMOD/FPGA_PMOD.html#PMOD_DVI), [TF Card PMod](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-PMOD/FPGA_PMOD.html#PMOD_TF-CARD), [DS2x2 PMod](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-PMOD/FPGA_PMOD.html#PMOD_DS2x2) and a [Tang SDRAM](https://wiki.sipeed.com/hardware/en/tang/tang-PMOD/FPGA_PMOD.html#TANG-40P-MODULE). 23 * The Tang Nano 20K is a tiny and popular FPGA dongle. The board also features 8MB of FPGA-gaming-friendly SDRAM memory. Be sure to get the [Tang Nano 20K Retro Gaming Kit](https://www.amazon.com/GW2AR-18-Computer-Debugger-Multiple-Emulator/dp/B0C5XLBQ6C), as it contains the necessary controllers and adapters. 24 25 ## Installation 26 27 A [step-by-step instructions](https://github.com/nand2mario/snestang/blob/main/doc/installation.md) is available for installation. Here are quick instructions for the more experienced, 28 29 * Tang Primer 25K needs 4 modules: Tang sdram, DVI, Dualshock2, SD and a pair of dualshock controllers. Currently these should cost ~$60 in total. Tang Nano 20K just needs controller adapters. Check [instructions](https://github.com/nand2mario/snestang/blob/main/doc/installation.md) for how to connect the modules / adapters. 30 * Download a NESTang release from [github](https://github.com/nand2mario/nestang/releases). The bitstream (`nestang_*.fs`) should be written to flash at address 0. The firmware (`firmware.bin`) should be written to 0x500000 (5MB). 31 * A MicroSD card to hold ROMs. 32 * Connect one or two DualShock2 controllers to the DS2 pmod. Or you can connect one USB gamepad to use the [experimental USB gamepad support](doc/usb_gamepad.md). The board only has one USB port. So use DS2 if you want two players. 33 * Insert the MicroSD card, connect an HDMI monitor or TV, and enjoy your games. 34 35 Version 0.4 also supports [tang primer 20k](doc/primer20k.md). 36 37 ## Development 38 39 If you want to generate the bitstream from source, see [Build Instructions](https://nand2mario.github.io/nestang-doc/dev/build_bitstream/). The recommended Gowin IDE version is 1.9.9 commercial (requires a free license). 40 41 [Usb_hid_host](https://github.com/nand2mario/usb_hid_host) was development so NESTang could support USB gamepads. Follow the link if you want to use it for your FPGA projects. It supports keyboards and mice too. 42 ### Code Snippet 5: README.md 45 See NESTang [changes.md](CHANGES.md). 46 47 Here are what I may work on when I get time. No promise though. <analysis>
The issue description is about NES controller wiring: the user says NES controller support was recently added and asks which pins they connect to, intending to build a connector with a breadboard and a voltage logic level converter.

From the provided snippets, there is no direct pinout, schematics, or HDL source shown. The only relevant clues are in the README, which references controller support and specifically mentions “DS2 pmod” and “controller adapters.” That means the likely root cause is not a runtime bug in the shown snippets, but missing or hard-to-find documentation about how NES controllers should be physically connected.

Possible causes to investigate:
1. The README may only mention controller support at a high level and omit the actual pin mapping.
2. The installation instructions referenced by README may contain the pinout, but that file is not included here.
3. The NES controller support might be implemented via the same adapter path as DualShock2 or via a specific Pmod header, and the exact pins could be defined in board- or adapter-specific documentation elsewhere.
4. Since the user asks about voltage level conversion, there may be missing electrical-interface details: whether the NES controller lines are 5V-tolerant, which signals are inputs/outputs, and which ground/VCC pins are expected.
5. The issue could involve ambiguity between Tang Nano 20K and Tang Primer 25K setups, since the README distinguishes them and each uses different controller hardware paths.

Related locations in the provided snippets are therefore the README sections that mention controller support, adapters, and installation guidance. Even though they do not contain the pinout, they are the only visible places that frame the controller-connection requirements and likely need inspection because they are the entry points for this information.
</analysis>
